name: Drowned Lantern

stars.name: The Lantern Remnant
stars.notes: The compressed core of a star that swelled and died eight billion years ago; it still burns hot enough to light its graveyard in eerie, sourceless blue.

planets.name: Wick
planets.notes: A scorched cinder orbiting close to the remnant; whatever it once was, the red giant phase left only fused glass and silence.

planets.name: Hullrock
planets.notes: A fractured world with ocean-cut canyons now frozen dry; geologists read its seabed terraces like tide marks on a hull and estimate the water was deep and warm for two billion years.

planets.name: Cold Wake
planets.notes: A frozen outer world whose ice shell may hide the system's last unfrozen sea; probe landings have been proposed every decade since the survey and quietly deferred each time.

asteroid_belts.name: Keel Debris Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: The pulverized metal heart of a destroyed planet, ground to glittering dust and shards; the richest salvage field this side of the Straits, and everyone's claim overlaps everyone else's.

stations.name: Salvor's Rest
stations.notes: A welded-together hulk of claim-shacks and processing rigs inside the debris ring; its crew works in shifts measured by oxygen margin rather than clocks.

faction_control.notes: No government bothers with a dead system; a rotating cast of scavenger syndicates holds de facto sway over the ring, honoring claims exactly as long as it is convenient.

history: Long before human charts, this system kept a warm ocean world under a yellow sun; when its star swelled into a red giant, that world boiled away, and what survived drifted as cinders around the white ember left behind.
A salvage tug seeking shelter from an Expanse storm stumbled onto the Keel Debris Ring and radioed back readings so rich that half the Straits' scavenger fleet arrived within a season.
Last year a dredger pulled up a machined alloy fragment of nonhuman manufacture from the ring, and the find has been disputed, suppressed, resold, and denied in roughly that order.
description: A dead star hangs in the dark like a lantern gone under, burning pale blue over its own wreckage. Three husks circle the remnant: a glassy cinder, a fractured rock carved by oceans that boiled away eons ago, and a frozen rim world. Between the second and third orbits glitters the Keel Debris Ring, the ground-up metal heart of a planet the dying star tore apart, bright enough to read by at close range.

Almost no one comes here, and those who do come for the ring. Sixty salvagers work Salvor's Rest amid the debris, cutting refined metal from planetary corpse-matter while syndicate tenders cycle ore out under minimal traffic manifests. There is no law beyond oxygen debt and grudges, and both are enforced strictly. For a low-value system, the Lantern keeps a surprising number of people lying about where they've been.

The mysteries here run deeper than salvage. Hullrock's frozen seabed shows erosion patterns that suggest something drained the ocean deliberately, the machined fragment from the ring matches nothing in any catalog, and Cold Wake's proposed probes keep being defunded by parties unknown. Old salvagers swear the debris ring is slowly rearranging itself, shard by shard, into a pattern. No one who says so aloud gets their contract renewed.
